# Just now, Google has released a new version of Gemini 4, which is targeted to surpass GPT-6.2 Sol, and the world model Genie 4 has also been opened to the public.

机器之心2026-11-19 08:09

The new intelligence located between Carbon and Hydrogen

Waking up, Google has once again released the Gemini 4 model.

Google has been putting heavy efforts into foundational models recently, rolling out models ranging from the highest intelligence to the highest efficiency nonstop, going all out to retake the top spot.

Following Carbon, Argon and Hydrogen, the "medium-sized" model Gemini 4 Neon that fills the gap between the highest intelligence and highest efficiency has arrived!

Demis Hassabis stated that Gemini 4 Neon, this medium-sized model, is "Alchemy at its finest".

In the Gemini 4 family, Carbon is the flagship, responsible for the most challenging long-horizon projects; Hydrogen is designed for high-frequency daily scenarios, prioritizing response speed. Neon is positioned between the two, "delivering cutting-edge reasoning capabilities for complex programming, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows, while being faster and more cost-effective".

Neon runs 3 times faster than Carbon, and costs only 60% of what Carbon does. It is priced at $3 per million input tokens, $15 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens as low as $0.15. It has a 1 million-token context window, and additionally supports 4 adjustable levels of thinking depth, allowing developers to flexibly switch between speed and reasoning depth according to task complexity.

Blog link: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-neon/

## Full Benchmark Test Results

Neon delivers quite well-rounded performance in third-party evaluations. In terms of comprehensive intelligence, it ranks 3rd with a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, only trailing behind larger, slower models; it ranks 2nd (70.9%) on the Vals Index, landing on the Pareto frontier.

In the brand-new Agent Arena Index, Neon took 2nd place (1336 points) with more than 4200 real-world agent sessions, and its steerability also ranks 2nd, which means that when users change their requirements midway, the model can adjust its direction more smoothly.

It has topped the rankings in a large number of enterprise and knowledge work evaluations. It ranks 1st in both the Legal Research Bench and Tax Agent Bench, and takes the top spot in most categories covered by Surge AI including finance, accounting, and spreadsheet modeling. It also takes 1st place on Zapier AutomationBench (56.3%) and Andon Labs' Vending-Bench 2 ($16,843). The latter is a test that simulates long-cycle business operations, which places high requirements on long-horizon planning capabilities. It scores 73.5% on the dense chart reading benchmark Chartography and 75.8% on Agents' Last Exam v1.1, on par with top-tier models.

In the field of scientific and mathematical reasoning, Neon won three first places: Terminal-Bench Science (70.5%), RiemannBench (84.0%) and HLE-Diamond (71.3%), all of which are the best in their class.

## Break Down Neon's Capabilities Item by Item

According to the official blog, Neon's new capabilities can be summarized into several major directions.

More accurate and stable code writing. Oriented to real production environments, Neon can handle multi-file debugging, refactoring and precise editing. Google specifically mentioned its "surgical edits" capability, which can perform targeted modifications on multi-file projects. The model has seen significant improvement in following multi-step instructions, and at the same time recorded the lowest fabrication rate to date in the internal Google Antigravity test.

1 million-token window supports multimodal inputs. Spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio, and video, Neon can process all these inputs in one context window at the same time, and output structured deliverables. "Neon has caught up with or even surpassed Carbon in overall quality, runs 3 times faster, and costs 40% less. It has found a convincing balance between accuracy, detail and speed."

Cybersecurity direction. This is a unique move in this Neon release. Google launched Neon for Cyber, covering the full chain of secure code writing, vulnerability discovery, vulnerability verification and vulnerability patching.

From the data, AutoBaxBench secure code generation reached SOTA (76%) at the difficulty level, comprehensively surpassing Carbon; WebExploitBench v1.2 penetration testing also achieved SOTA (51.26%), with the cost only half of that of competing large models; SEC-bench Pro vulnerability discovery reached SOTA (90.5%), with the cost per challenge about half of similar products; CWE-bench v2 vulnerability patching reached 70.7%, 3.4% higher than Carbon. Neon for Cyber will be opened to trusted security defenders through the Fairwind Program in the next few days.

Security alignment, almost "zero cheating". Google has made heavy investments in security. The Terminal-Bench 4.0 cheating rate is 0.0%, on par with Carbon; only 2.45% of tasks show shortcut behavior in the coding cheating evaluation, the lowest in the entire Gemini 4 series; the improper behavior rate in the agent security suite is 0.09%, and the honesty evaluation pass rate is 99.2%. In Gray Swan's indirect prompt injection benchmark, Neon achieved a 0.0% attack success rate at the highest thinking level. Compared with Carbon, Neon reduced "under-servicing" by 43%-56%, and "unauthorized operation" by 15%-35%. At the same time, it hardly rejects legitimate tasks, only rejecting 1.98% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, and the rejection rate on Terminal-Bench-Science is 0%.

Upgrades on the consumer side as well. In the Gemini app, Neon brings higher quality writing output, can read uploaded content such as spreadsheets, PDFs and photos more accurately, and can also access Gmail and Docs to obtain relevant information. The Tasks function is now powered by Neon, which is faster and more quota-efficient when handling complex multi-step tasks.

Gemini 4 Neon has begun rolling out. Developers can build applications in Google AI Studio and Android Studio via the paid tier of the Gemini API, and Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can try it out in Google Antigravity. Enterprise users can access it via the Gemini for Business API or the model dropdown menu. On the consumer side, Pro and Ultra subscribers can directly switch to Neon in the model selector of the Gemini app. Neon for Cyber for cybersecurity scenarios will be pushed to trusted defenders through the Fairwind Program in the next few days.

## The world model Genie 4 is finally launched

On October 28, Google DeepMind officially announced the latest generation world model Genie 4, calling it "the most realistic and interactive world model to date".

After waiting for more than half a month, Google finally announced that Genie 4 is officially available.

Blog link: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/genie-4-now-available-project-genie/

Genie 4 is Google's most realistic and interactive world model to date. Its core new capability is "mid-session prompting", which means you can use natural language to change the environment at any time while you are browsing the world. You can switch the weather, spawn a character, change the direction of the plot, and all changes happen in real time in the current scene.

Another first-time capability is native audio. The world generated by Genie 4 comes with built-in sound, and the sound will automatically adapt to scene changes, including everything from ambient sound effects to character dialogues, filling in the "auditory" puzzle piece.

Genie 4 focuses on the highest fidelity, while Genie 3 will remain available in the model selector of Project Genie, oriented to longer exploration and panoramic scenarios.

While launching Genie 4 this time, Google also launched Project Genie Agent. Previously, creating a world required you to carefully organize prompts, but now it has become a conversation. You describe the world you want in natural language, and the agent will schedule Google's multimodal model portfolio to generate the initial visual picture to establish the visual style of the world, along with custom-made background music.

What's more interesting is that the Gemini model can observe the screen content synchronously while you explore the world, actively pop up suggestions on "where to go next", or automatically trigger in-world events according to your journey.

# 刚刚，谷歌Gemini 4再发新款，对标超越GPT-6.2 Sol，世界模型Genie 4也已开放

机器之心·2026年11月19日 08:09

位于 Carbon 和 Hydrogen 之间的新智能

一觉醒来，谷歌又双叒叕发 Gemini 4 模型了。

谷歌最近一直在基础模型上发力，从最高智能到最高效率的模型不停发布，为了重返王座真是拼了。

在 Carbon、Argon、Hydrogen 之后，填补最高智能和最高效率之间的「中杯」模型 Gemini 4 Neon 登场！

Demis Hassabis 称，Gemini 4 Neon 这一中杯模型，是「Alchemy at its finest（炼金术的杰作）」。

Gemini 4 家族中，Carbon 是旗舰，负责最难的长程项目；Hydrogen 面向日常高频场景，追求的是响应速度。Neon 的定位在二者中间，「在复杂编程、分析推理和生产级企业工作流上提供前沿推理能力，同时更快、更省」。

Neon 速度是 Carbon 的 3 倍，成本只有 Carbon 的 60%。定价每百万输入 token 3 美元，每百万输出 token 15 美元，缓存输入 token 低至 0.15 美元，上下文窗口 100 万 token，另外支持 4 档可调的思考深度，开发者可以按任务复杂度灵活切换速度和推理深度。

博客链接：https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-neon/

## 全面跑分

Neon 在第三方评测上的表现相当全面。综合智能方面，它在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 上以 61 分排到第 3，仅落后于更大、更慢的模型；在 Vals Index 上排第 2（70.9%），落在帕累托前沿上。

在全新的 Agent Arena Index 中，Neon 凭借 4200 余个真实世界智能体会话拿下第 2（1336 分），可操控性（steerability）同样排第 2，意味着用户中途改口时，模型能更干净地调整方向。

企业和知识工作类的评测更是大面积刷榜。Legal Research Bench 和 Tax Agent Bench 两项第 1，Surge AI 覆盖的金融、会计、电子表格建模等多个类目也大多排在第 1。Zapier AutomationBench 第 1（56.3%），Andon Labs 的 Vending-Bench 2 同样第 1（$16,843），后者是一个模拟长周期商业经营的测试，对长程规划能力要求很高。密集图表阅读基准 Chartography 得分 73.5%，Agents' Last Exam v1.1 得分 75.8%，与头部模型持平。

科学和数学推理方向上，Neon 拿下了 Terminal-Bench Science（70.5%）、RiemannBench（84.0%）和 HLE-Diamond（71.3%）三项第一，均为同类最佳。

## 逐项拆解 Neon 能力

根据官方博客，Neon 的新能力可以归纳为几个大方向。

写代码，更准更稳。Neon 面向真实生产环境，能处理多文件调试、重构和精准编辑。谷歌特别提到了它的「surgical edits（手术式编辑）」能力，能对多文件项目做定点修改。模型在多步骤指令遵循上有明显提升，同时在内部 Google Antigravity 测试中录得了迄今为止最低的编造率（fabrication rate）。

100 万 token 窗口拿下多模态。电子表格、PDF、图表、音频、视频，Neon 可以在一个上下文窗口里同时消化这些输入，输出结构化的交付物。「Neon 在整体质量上追平甚至超过了 Carbon，速度快 3 倍，成本降低 40%。它在准确性、细节和速度之间找到了令人信服的平衡。」

网络安全方向。这是 Neon 本次发布中一个独特的动作。谷歌推出了 Neon for Cyber，覆盖安全代码编写、漏洞发现、漏洞验证和漏洞修补的完整链条。

从数据看，AutoBaxBench 安全代码生成在困难级别达到 SOTA（76%），全面超越 Carbon；WebExploitBench v1.2 渗透测试同样 SOTA（51.26%），成本仅为竞品大模型的一半；SEC-bench Pro 漏洞发现 SOTA（90.5%），单挑战成本约为同类的一半；CWE-bench v2 漏洞修补 70.7%，比 Carbon 提升 3.4%。Neon for Cyber 将在未来几天内通过 Fairwind Program 向受信任的安全防御人员开放。

安全对齐，几乎「零作弊」。谷歌在安全性上下了重注。Terminal-Bench 4.0 作弊率 0.0%，与 Carbon 持平；编码作弊评估中仅 2.45% 的任务出现走捷径行为，是 Gemini 4 全系列最低；智能体安全套件中不当行为率 0.09%，诚实评估通过率 99.2%。在 Gray Swan 的间接提示注入基准中，Neon 在最高思考级别上达到了 0.0% 的攻击成功率。对比 Carbon，Neon 将「服务不足」降低了 43%-56%，「越权操作」降低了 15%-35%。同时它在合法任务上几乎不拒绝，Terminal-Bench 4.0 上仅拒 1.98%，Terminal-Bench-Science 上拒绝率为 0%。

消费者端也有升级。在 Gemini 应用中，Neon 带来了更高质量的写作输出，能更精准地读取电子表格、PDF 和照片等上传内容，还可以接入 Gmail 和 Docs 获取相关信息。Tasks 功能现在由 Neon 驱动，处理复杂多步骤任务时更快更省额度。

Gemini 4 Neon 已经开始滚动上线。开发者可以通过 Gemini API 付费层级在 Google AI Studio 和 Android Studio 中构建应用，Google AI Pro 和 Ultra 订阅用户能在 Google Antigravity 中试用。企业用户走 Gemini for Business 的 API 或模型下拉菜单。消费者端，Pro 和 Ultra 订阅用户可以在 Gemini 应用的模型选择器里直接切换到 Neon。网络安全方向的 Neon for Cyber 会在未来几天内通过 Fairwind Program 推送给受信任的防御人员。

## 世界模型 Genie 4 终于上线

10 月 28 日，谷歌 DeepMind 官宣最新一代世界模型 Genie 4，称其为「迄今为止最逼真、交互性最强的世界模型」。

经过超过半月的等待，谷歌终于宣布 Genie 4 正式上线可用。

博客链接：https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/genie-4-now-available-project-genie/

Genie 4 是谷歌目前最逼真、最具交互性的世界模型。它最核心的新能力是「mid-session prompting」，也就是在你浏览世界的过程中，随时用自然语言改变环境。你可以切换天气、投放一个角色、改变剧情走向，所有变化实时发生在当前画面中。

另一个首次出现的能力是原生音频（native audio）。Genie 4 生成的世界自带声音，而且声音会随场景变化自动适配，从环境音效到角色对话都包含在内，补上了「听觉」这块拼图。

Genie 4 主打最高保真度，Genie 3 则在 Project Genie 的模型选择器中继续保留，面向更长时间的探索和全景场景。

本次谷歌在上线 Genie 4 的同时，也上线了Project Genie Agent。以前创建一个世界需要你精心组织 prompt，现在变成了一场对话。你用自然语言描述你想要的世界，智能体会调度谷歌的多模态模型组合，生成初始视觉画面来建立世界的视觉风格，同时配上量身定制的背景音乐。

更有意思的是，Gemini 模型可以在你探索世界时同步观察屏幕内容，主动弹出「下一步去哪」的建议，或者根据你的旅程自动触发世界内事件。

问AI · 新模型擅多模态输入却非生成，能力边界如何划定？

Gemini 4 Neon

凤凰网科技讯 北京时间11月19日，谷歌公司在周三发布了最新模型Gemini 4 Neon，这是该公司在一个月时间内发布的第四款Gemini模型。谷歌称，Gemini 4 Neon具备前沿水平的智能能力，能够快速端到端地完成复杂的软件工程、知识工作和科学研究任务。

在高强度思考模式下，Neon在Artificial Analysis智能指数中的得分为61分，在同类模型中排名靠前，总榜排名第三，仅落后于规模更大、运行速度更慢的模型。在Vals Index榜单中，Neon排名第二，并处于帕累托前沿(兼顾性能和成本)。

除了持续提升模型本身的能力，谷歌也在不断改善模型的易用性。在最新的Agent Arena Index榜单中，Neon的可操控性排名第二，能够灵活适应用户在任务执行过程中提出的修正要求。Neon在多步骤指令遵循方面同样表现出色，并在遏制模型编造(幻觉)方面延续了谷歌的持续进展。在Google Antigravity内部测试中，Neon的幻觉率创下最低水平。

Neon的各项跑分

Neon提供约100万个Token的上下文窗口，最多可生成100万个Token的输出内容。它支持处理文本、图像、视频、音频和PDF文件，并支持以下功能：计算机操控、代码执行、文件搜索，以及通过Google搜索和Google地图获取信息并进行事实核验。不过，该模型不支持图像和音频生成。

该模型今日起通过API正式开放，定价为每百万输入Token 3美元、每百万输出Token 15美元，高于Carbon和Argon最初每百万输入Token 2美元、每百万输出Token 10美元的定价(12月1日起将涨至4美元和20美元)。这一价格也是Hydrogen(每百万输入Token 1.50美元、每百万输出Token 7.50美元)的两倍。

与此同时，谷歌还宣布，公司最新世界模型Genie 4已经上线。这是谷歌最先进的世界模型，可用于生成可交互的3D世界。

此前，Genie 4仅以研究预览版形式开放，此次作为Project Genie重大更新的一部分正式推出，目前已向Google AI Ultra订阅用户开放。

Genie 4允许用户通过文本指令实时改变虚拟世界，例如调整天气、角色或故事情节。该模型还能够原生生成实时音效，并根据场景变化自动调整。(作者/箫雨)

# Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Neon at $3/$15 per million tokens

Google says Neon ranks third on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and is rolling out through its API, business offering, Antigravity and the Gemini app.

Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November 2026, adding a model for software engineering, knowledge work and science to its Gemini 4 line. The company says Neon is rolling out through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, Gemini for business, Google Antigravity for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers.

## Key points

- Neon costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.
- Google reports a score of 61 and third place on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at Neon’s xhigh thinking level.
- Crypto Briefing reports estimates of roughly 17% lower cost per task than Gemini 4 Carbon, or approximately 32% at the default high thinking level.

## Neon’s $3 input and $15 output rates

Google prices Neon at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. Cached input costs $0.15 per million tokens, a 95% discount on the standard input rate. Those prices give developers separate rates for material sent to the model and material it generates, rather than a fixed charge for each completed task.

The model has a 1 million-token context window: the space available for material supplied to it in one request. Google says Neon can work across spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio and video within that window and produce structured outputs from them. The window describes how much material can be put before the model, rather than a score for the quality of its answer.

Reviewing paperwork could bring a long PDF, its charts and an audio recording into one request, provided the material fits the stated window. The requested output could be a structured account of those inputs, the kind of work Google says Neon performs.

Crypto Briefing reported that a post on X estimated Neon’s cost per task at about 17% below Gemini 4 Carbon’s, rising to approximately 32% below Carbon’s at the default high thinking level. Thinking level governs how much reasoning the model does before answering, so the setting affects the amount of work billed for a task.

Neon is the fourth Gemini 4 model, after Argon, Carbon and Hydrogen. AI Affairs previously reported Carbon’s wider release and a preview of agent swarms, then Hydrogen’s launch and model switching in Antigravity. Google is presenting Neon as an option for complex work in which both the result and the cost of repeated calls count.

## Neon scores 61 on Artificial Analysis

Google says Neon scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh thinking level, placing third overall behind models it describes as larger and slower. That is a result at a specified reasoning setting, whereas the reported per-task saving of approximately 32% against Carbon uses Neon’s default high setting.

On the Vals Index, Google reports a score of 70.9% and second place. It also reports a score of 1336 and second place on the Agent Arena Index, based on more than 4,200 real-world agent sessions. Google says Neon ranked second there for steerability, which it describes as adapting to corrections made partway through a task. The session count belongs to that agent evaluation, rather than to the other rankings.

Google reports first-place results on Legal Research Bench and Tax Agent Bench. In scientific and mathematical testing, it reports 70.5% on Terminal-Bench Science, 84.0% on RiemannBench and 71.3% on HLE-Diamond.

## Antigravity lifts Neon’s SWE-sweep score to 39.0%

For coding, Google says Neon can work through long tasks involving tools and multiple files, either on its own or directing parallel Hydrogen subagents in Google Antigravity. Its description of the model’s behaviour includes fewer repeated file reads, progress updates during a task and the ability to compress earlier context in long sessions.

Neon scores 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and 46.2% on FrontierCode 2.0 at its default high setting. On SWE-sweep, it reports 12.8% using the mini-SWE harness and 39.0% in Google Antigravity. A harness is the software environment in which a model attempts the test, so the Antigravity result includes the way that environment lets Neon carry out the work. Google also places Neon first on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, with a score of 58.6.

Google says Neon can make targeted changes across repositories for debugging and refactoring. It also reports its lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing, an assessment conducted within the company rather than one of the named external coding evaluations.

# Meta AI Privacy Guide: What You Can Disable and What Stays On

Meta AI privacy settings can restrict some data uses, but they can’t permanently turn off the assistant across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger. Meta AI is Meta’s artificial intelligence assistant,…

Meta AI privacy settings can restrict some data uses, but they can’t permanently turn off the assistant across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger. Meta AI is Meta’s artificial intelligence assistant, available across its services and in a dedicated app. That distinction matters: changing one setting may limit a feature without stopping other AI functions.

## Why Meta AI Privacy Cannot Be Switched Off Everywhere

There’s no verified universal switch for turning off Meta AI across Meta’s apps. Instead, each control applies to certain features, data types or conversations. Some also depend on your region, device or account.

For example, muting a chat changes what you see, but doesn’t by itself prevent data use. Meta’s Help Center explains how to manage information in the Meta AI app and on Meta.ai. You can use those controls to manage or delete chats and media. An objection request works differently: it asks Meta to limit certain uses of information, but it doesn’t switch off the assistant.

## How to Find Meta AI Privacy Settings

In the Meta AI app, tap Menu in the top-left corner. Choose Settings, then Data & privacy and Manage your information. On Meta.ai, click your profile picture in the bottom-left corner, then follow Settings → Data & privacy → Manage your information.

Meta’s information management instructions explain how these controls work. They’re spread across products, so check the app where you use each feature. Availability and menu wording can vary; if a setting doesn’t appear in your account, don’t assume it’s available. Make one change at a time, and check what it covers before making another.

## Meta AI Privacy Controls You Can Change

These options control individual features; they aren’t a permanent, account-wide opt-out. Each comes with a limit or trade-off:

- Meta AI app prompt suggestions: Open Settings → Data & privacy → Suggesting your prompts on other apps, then switch off the Facebook and Instagram options. On mobile, the label may say Suggesting your vibes on other apps. This stops cross-app suggestions, not Meta AI itself.
- Facebook comment summaries: Go to Settings → Audience and visibility → Posts, then turn off Allow comment summaries on your posts. Not every user will see this control.
- WhatsApp chat privacy: Open the info page for a chat or group, then enable Advanced Chat Privacy. This setting applies to that conversation only, not your entire account.
- Ray-Ban Meta glasses: In the Meta AI app, go to Settings → Meta AI and switch off Store visual data from AI experiences. Meta’s glasses data guidance says this setting prevents covered future visual data from being stored or used to improve products. Some features, including visual reminders, may be limited. Voice interactions and images shared in other apps aren’t covered.
- Meta AI conversations: You can mute or delete the conversation in WhatsApp or Messenger, or delete it on Instagram. That may reduce notifications or remove the chat from view, but it won’t disable the assistant.

## What an Objection Request Changes—and What It Does Not

If the option is available for your account and region, you can use Meta’s objection process to request limits on certain AI-related uses of your information. Availability and scope depend on your circumstances. The request won’t undo training that’s already complete, and it may not cover information other people post about you.

It can reduce future use of covered data, but can’t guarantee that all information about you will be excluded. Turning off a feature may also make it less convenient or reduce its functionality. For instance, disabling visual-data storage can limit visual reminders, while muting a chatbot changes notifications only. Some third-party guides mention search-bar or message-suggestion switches, but their general availability hasn’t been established; rely on the controls in your app. Meta AI privacy settings offer targeted limits, not a permanent master switch: choose the control that matches the data or feature you want to restrict.

## Where are Meta AI privacy settings in the app?

In the Meta AI app, tap Menu, then Settings, Data & privacy, and Manage your information. On Meta.ai, click your profile picture, then follow Settings → Data & privacy → Manage your information.

## What does Advanced Chat Privacy do in WhatsApp?

It applies to the specific WhatsApp chat or group where you enable it, not your entire account.

## Can you turn off Meta AI across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger?

There’s no verified universal switch for turning off Meta AI across Meta’s apps. Individual controls apply to certain features, data types or conversations.

# 2026 年阿里云 Qwen4-Max 是什么模型？能力边界与落地场景一次讲清

2026-11-19 23

举报

简介： Qwen4-Max 是 2026年 Qwen4 系列的旗舰基座，2.4T 总参数、71B 激活、原生视觉、百万 Token 上下文，配合 GDN 与 QSA 混合注意力把长上下文的读取成本压了下来。它的价值不在单点分数，而在"能把长任务跑完并交付成品"这件事上，同时把单任务成本拉低了近六成。适用边界也很清楚：需要私有化部署或模型微调的项目，当前并不适用。选型时先看任务形态，再看成本结构，比只看榜单分数更有意义。

2026年11月，阿里云正式发布通义千问新一代旗舰基座模型 Qwen4-Max，并同步上线百炼平台。与前代旗舰相比，这一代的重点不再是单项能力刷榜，而是把优化方向压在专业工作场景的长链路任务上：更长的上下文、更少的 Token 消耗、更低的单任务成本，以及能持续交付可用成果的执行方式。本文从模型定位、架构特征、能力清单、评测表现、适用场景、接入方式六个层面做完整解析。文中数据取自官方模型卡与公开评测材料，具体规格以百炼模型页实时信息为准。

## 一、模型定位：从问答工具转向可交付工作的基座

Qwen4-Max 的官方定位是新一代旗舰多模态智能体基座模型。它的设计假设很明确：企业里真正有价值的工作，很少能塞进一次对话。这些任务往往持续数小时、跨越几十个工具、涉及上千页资料，最终必须产出一份团队能直接使用的东西——一份可运行的代码、一份可评审的方案、一张可交付的设计稿。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

因此它的能力取向围绕三件事展开：第一，能稳定调用专业工具链，而不只是生成文本；第二，能把长任务推进到终点，中途不丢上下文、不跑偏；第三，交付的是成品而非中间回答。官方把这套机制命名为 Live Delivery（渐进交付）：在长任务开始时先给出一版可用的初版，之后持续迭代提交改进版本，让团队在任务运行过程中就能评审和纠偏，而不是等到最后才发现方向错了。

这一定位决定了它与轻量对话模型的分工。日常问答、简单文案，用更小的模型成本更低；而跨文档分析、多文件工程改造、长流程智能体，才是 Qwen4-Max 的合理使用区间。

## 二、架构特征：2.4T 参数与百万上下文如何兼顾效率

Qwen4-Max 总参数规模为 2.4 万亿（2.4T），单 Token 仅激活 710 亿（71B），另外配置 3280 亿（328B）的 N-gram Embedding 参数。总参数大、激活参数小，是典型的稀疏混合专家路线，目的是在保住能力上限的同时压住单次推理的算力开销。官方数据显示，每个 Token 的激活参数比上一代减少约 25%。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

支撑百万级上下文的，是三项架构改动：

GDN + QSA 混合注意力。 每四层中，三层使用 Gated DeltaNet（GDN），把历史信息压缩成固定大小的状态，使 KV 缓存不随上下文长度线性增长；剩下一层使用 Qwen Sparse Attention（QSA），通过轻量索引定位关键段落。官方给出的效果是百万 Token 读取速度提升 7 倍以上。这一点对长文档、长代码库场景意义很大——上下文再长，显存与延迟也不会失控。

GR 门控残差。 把单通道残差流展宽为 4 条并行分支，配合动态读写门控，增强跨层信息传递。工程上的直接收益是 2.4T 规模训练全程平稳，没有出现损失突增（Loss Spike）。这类改动不出现在能力指标里，但决定了大模型能否稳定训到目标规模。

N-gram Embedding。 单独配置 328B 的 N-gram 嵌入参数，用于强化高频片段的表征，对代码、术语密集的专业文本有直接帮助。

规格层面，Qwen4-Max 上下文长度为 100 万 Token，最大输入 991,808 Token，最大输出 131,072 Token；开启思考模式时，最大输入 983,616 Token、最大输出 262,144 Token，最大思维链长度同为 262,144 Token。输入模态覆盖文本、图像、视频，输出为文本。原生视觉并非后期拼接的适配层，工程图纸、医疗影像、长视频都可以直接作为输入。

## 三、能力清单：哪些能做，哪些不做

官方模型卡列出的支持项包括：流式输出、深度思考、并行工具调用、联网搜索、前缀补全、Function Calling、思维链摘要与加密、结构化输出（JSON Object 与 JSON Schema）、显式缓存与隐式缓存、批量推理。接口层面兼容 OpenAI Chat Completions、Responses、Anthropic Messages 与 DashScope，迁移成本较低，已有 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 风格调用的项目大多只需换 Base URL 与模型 ID。

深度思考默认开启，可通过 reasoning_effort 调节推理力度。这里有一个必须注意的工程细节：从预览版开始，max_tokens 与 max_completion_tokens 语义等价，二者共同限制"思考内容 + 最终回答"的总量。如果沿用过去只为回答预留上限的写法，开启思考后输出会被提前截断。迁移时应当为思考与回答共同预留额度。

明确不支持的项同样重要：模型调优不支持，模型部署不支持。也就是说，Qwen4-Max 只能以 API 方式调用，不能私有化微调后自行部署。对数据必须留在自有环境的项目，这条限制需要在选型阶段就确认清楚。

## 四、评测表现：能力提升与成本下降同时发生

官方公布的 Work360 评测中，Qwen4-Max 得分 52.69，上一代为 47.74。在相同推理力度下，单任务 Token 消耗明显下降：Work360 在 Xhigh 与 High 两档分别减少约 24% 与 35%，Terminal-Bench 4.0 分别减少约 48% 与 49%。综合结果是平均单任务成本比上一代下降 58%。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

中文通用能力侧，2026年11月的 SuperCLUE 测评中 Qwen4-Max 取得 61.61 分，进入国内第一梯队，较上一版本提升 18.39 分。分项上，幻觉控制 73.61 分、提升 40.56 分；超长上下文 77.80 分、提升 33.42 分；智能体编程 57.69 分、提升 15.38 分。更值得关注的是稳定性：上一代在同一测试中超时率为 69.23%，新模型超时率降至 0%，全部试题跑完。按测试的 Token 开销与定价折算，平均每题成本约 1.90 元，较上一代下降约 87%。

这组数据的含义是：能力提升之外，单位任务的调用成本出现了数量级变化。对高频跑智能体流程的团队来说，成本项的变化往往比分数更能决定项目是否跑得起来。

## 五、适用场景：六类任务最匹配

编程开发与工程改造。 支持多文件读取、工具调用与结构化输出，配合百万上下文可直接把整个代码库放进一次会话。Terminal-Bench 上 Token 消耗下降近半，意味着批量重构、批量测试生成这类任务的账单压力明显减轻。

前端与设计还原。 原生视觉可直接读取设计稿、截图、原型图，输出可运行的页面代码，适合设计到开发的衔接环节。

办公与文档处理。 长报告、合同、财报、会议材料，单份即可覆盖在上下文内，不需要切块摘要再拼接，减少信息在切分过程中丢失的问题。结构化输出可以直接产出 JSON，方便对接下游系统。

复杂智能体与流程自动化。 并行工具调用、联网搜索、Function Calling 齐备，适合需要串联检索、计算、写文件、调用内部接口的长链路流程。Live Delivery 机制让长任务可以边跑边交付，便于中途校正。

专业视觉理解。 工程图纸、医疗影像、长视频分析，属于原生视觉的典型用例，无需额外接视觉模型。

长文档审阅与合规核查。 幻觉控制分项的大幅提升，加上长上下文能力，适合条款比对、事实核验这类对准确性敏感的工作。

反过来，不适合的场景也要说清：单轮简单问答、短文案润色、固定模板填表，用旗舰模型的成本没有必要；需要私有化部署或模型微调的项目，Qwen4-Max 目前不提供这两条路径。

## 六、接入与计费：Token Plan 是唯一入口

Qwen4-Max 通过百炼接入，预览版 qwen4-max-preview 仅支持 Token Plan，不开放按量计费。预览期为 2026年11月11日 10:00 至 11月25日 24:00（UTC+8），期间模型能力持续迭代，预览结束后下线，正式版 qwen4-max 已上线，建议直接使用正式版。

调用方式上，先开通 Token Plan 个人版或团队版，获取套餐专用 API Key（前缀 sk-sp），使用套餐专用 Base URL：
export DASHSCOPE_API_KEY="sk-sp-xxxxxxxx"
export BASE_URL="[https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com](https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com)"

          AI 代码解读

以 OpenAI 兼容方式发起一次带思考的调用：
curl "$BASE_URL/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DASHSCOPE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen4-max",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "分析这份接口文档的字段变更风险"}],
    "reasoning_effort": "high",
    "max_completion_tokens": 8192
  }'

          AI 代码解读

用 SDK 时同样只需替换模型与地址：
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="sk-sp-xxxxxxxx",
    base_url="[https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1](https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1)",
)
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen4-max",
    messages=[{
   "role": "user", "content": "把这段 SQL 改写成可并行的版本"}],
    reasoning_effort="high",
    max_completion_tokens=8192,
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

          AI 代码解读

计费侧需要记住三点：Token Plan 以 Credits 统一计量，一份订阅额度可覆盖平台内多款模型，套餐额度按月重置、不结转；套餐专用 Key 与通用 Key、其他订阅计划不通用；部署地域为华北2（北京），跨境业务需评估访问链路。

## 七、选型建议

判断是否需要 Qwen4-Max，可以先回答三个问题：任务是否需要跨几十页文档或整个代码库？是否需要在一次会话里连续调用多个工具直到产出成品？是否对事实准确性高度敏感？三项中命中两项以上，旗舰档才值得；否则更小的模型配外部工具组合，性价比通常更好。对已经在用上一代旗舰的团队，迁移的收益主要落在两处：单任务 Token 消耗下降带来的账单缩减，以及超时率归零带来的流程稳定性。迁移风险集中在输出预算参数——务必按"思考 + 回答"合计的口径重新设定上限，否则会出现长任务被截断、看起来像模型能力不足的误判。

## 八、总结

Qwen4-Max 是 2026年 Qwen4 系列的旗舰基座，2.4T 总参数、71B 激活、原生视觉、百万 Token 上下文，配合 GDN 与 QSA 混合注意力把长上下文的读取成本压了下来。它的价值不在单点分数，而在"能把长任务跑完并交付成品"这件事上，同时把单任务成本拉低了近六成。适用边界也很清楚：需要私有化部署或模型微调的项目，当前并不适用。选型时先看任务形态，再看成本结构，比只看榜单分数更有意义。

# Claude Opus 5.5 vs GLM-5.4: The Cheap Token Is Not the Cheap Task

Author
jinhao.song
Date Published

Latest models · 20View all models →

Benchmarks: Artificial Analysis · updated daily

Back to all posts

The most expensive mistake in model selection is comparing price lists instead of finished tasks. Claude Opus 5.5 costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output. GLM-5.3 — the model Z.ai actually ships, and the one anyone typing "GLM-5.4" is looking for — costs $1.40 and $4.40. On the sticker, the Chinese open-weights model is roughly a fifth of the price. On Artificial Analysis's own measurement of what a task costs to complete, the gap collapses to 2×. That collapse, not the price list, is the story of this comparison.

First, the name. GLM-5.4 does not exist. Z.ai's documentation index lists GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash as the current text models, the lab's Hugging Face organisation has no repository with "5.4" in it, and a full-text search of the Hub on 19 November returns nothing. The number is a search term, not a release. GLM-5.3 shipped in August 2026 — 18 August by Artificial Analysis's release date, with the weights on the Hub from 25 August — and it is the model every claim below is about.

## What GLM-5.3 is, and what it costs

GLM-5.3 is Z.ai's open-weights text flagship. It uses the same base model as GLM-5.2, with every gain coming from post-training, which is why the licence and the architecture are unchanged and why the improvements concentrate in exactly two places: complex coding and long-horizon agentic work. It has a 1M-token context, 128K max output, text-only input, and reasoning that cannot be switched off — three effort levels, low, high and max, defaulting to max.

• Price — Claude Opus 5.5 $4.00 input / $20.00 output / $0.20 cache read vs GLM-5.3 $1.40 / $4.40.

• Weights — closed API only vs Apache-style open release on Hugging Face, downloadable and self-hostable.

• Context — 1M tokens both, 128K max output both.

• Effort control — Opus 5.5 runs adaptive thinking that cannot be disabled, default medium vs GLM-5.3 reasoning always on, default max.

• Intelligence Index — 59.1 vs 31.7 on the v5.0.1 revision, a 27.4-point gap.

• Cost per Index task — $10.04 vs $5.01, a 2× gap, not the 4.5× the sticker implies.

• Modality — text and image input vs text only.

## Why a 4.5× price advantage becomes a 2× cost advantage

Artificial Analysis ran both models through the same Index suite and counted the tokens each one spent. Claude Opus 5.5 generated 218M output tokens across the suite. GLM-5.3 generated 135M. That is not the direction most people expect — the expensive model is the more verbose one here — but the ratio that matters is against the price, and GLM-5.3's 1.6× token advantage does not come close to covering its 4.5× per-token advantage in the other direction.

Run the arithmetic the way a budget does. On a task where both models spend the same number of tokens, GLM-5.3 is 4.5× cheaper. In practice GLM-5.3 spends about 0.62 tokens for every one Opus 5.5 spends, so the effective ratio lands near 2.8× before input tokens, and the measured per-task figure of $5.01 against $10.04 puts it at 2×. Still a real saving — roughly half — but half is a different decision from a fifth. A team that budgeted on the sticker and got a 2× bill will have built the wrong business case.

There is a second-order effect worth flagging because it caught out more than one team: GLM-5.3's reasoning defaults to max. A migration that only swaps the model ID and leaves the reasoning default untouched gets the most expensive and slowest configuration of the model, which is precisely where the verbosity comes from. Z.ai's own migration note is explicit that disabling reasoning is no longer supported and that low must be set deliberately.

## The capability gap is real, and it is not uniform

A 27-point index gap sounds disqualifying, and for general knowledge work it nearly is. But the per-benchmark numbers separate the two models along a line that matters more than the composite. All figures below are Artificial Analysis's, same harness, both at their highest effort setting.

• Terminal-Bench 4.0 — 59.6% vs 41.9%. An 18-point gap on agentic terminal work.

• FrontierCode-AA 2.0 — 46.4% vs 21.6%. Opus 5.5 more than doubles GLM-5.3.

• Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 — 59.0% vs 9.5%. The largest gap on the board, and a rout.

• HLE-Diamond — 67.9% vs 17.9%.

• AA-Omniscience — 48.1 at 65.5% accuracy vs 6.0 at 32.3% accuracy.

• GDPval-AA v2.1 — 1866 Elo vs 1655, the narrowest gap of the set at 211 points.

• ITBench-SRE — 38.2% vs 46.1%, one of the few places GLM-5.3 wins.

• LCR (long-context reasoning) — 84.7% vs 79.7%.

The pattern is that GLM-5.3 holds up on long-context reasoning and on site-reliability tasks, and falls apart on science-heavy terminal work and knowledge recall. If your workload is document analysis over a long context, the 27-point composite overstates the difference. If it is agentic coding on unfamiliar repositories — which is what both vendors market — the composite understates it.

## The vendor table Z.ai publishes compares Opus 4.8, not Opus 5.5

Worth knowing before you trust any GLM-versus-Claude number you find in a chart. Z.ai's GLM-5.3 model card carries a benchmark table with an "Opus 4.8" column and a "Fable 5 (w/ fallback)" column. Claude Opus 5.5, released five weeks after GLM-5.3, does not appear in it. That is not dishonesty — the table was built when 5.3 shipped and Opus 5.5 did not exist yet — but it does mean the comparison most people are searching for has never been published by either vendor, and the only same-harness numbers available are the independent ones above.

Z.ai's own numbers do carry one claim worth taking seriously, because it points at the open-weights model's genuine strength: on CyberGym, its vulnerability-discovery benchmark, GLM-5.3 scores 84.5 against Opus 4.8's 78.1. The card describes the gain as "emergent" — cyber capability scaled faster than the team expected as post-training scaled — and the exploitation benchmarks more than double from GLM-5.2. Anthropic published an analysis of GLM-5.3's cyber capabilities on 29 September, which is not a thing vendors usually do about a competitor's open-weights release. If your work is defensive security tooling, that is the one axis where the open model is genuinely ahead, and it is also the axis where the open weights matter most: you can run the classifier on your own infrastructure rather than sending exploit-adjacent prompts to someone's API.

## Where the open weights actually change the decision

Everything above is a capability and cost comparison, and on both counts Claude Opus 5.5 wins for most work. The reason GLM-5.3 still gets deployed is neither: it is that a 5.3-family model downloads, runs behind your own gateway, and never leaves your network.

Three concrete situations where that outweighs 27 index points. Regulated data that cannot cross a jurisdiction boundary, where the choice is GLM-5.3 or nothing. High-volume classification where a 300M-parameter fine-tune of the base beats the general model on your labels at a fraction of the per-call cost. And cyber-adjacent tooling, where the benchmark advantage and the self-hosting requirement point the same way.

For everything else the honest recommendation is to keep the routing decision cheap. Both models are on one OrcaRouter key — anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 and z-ai/glm-5.3 — at 0% markup on provider list price, which matters more for the Z.ai side than the Anthropic side because Z.ai repriced this line twice in 2026. Route the high-volume, low-stakes passes to GLM-5.3 and the planning loop to Opus 5.5, and let failover cover the case where the cheap tier's provider has a bad afternoon. The routing DSL makes that a config change rather than two integrations, and the blended per-task figure is the one to put in the budget rather than either sticker.

## The answer, with the name settled

Claude Opus 5.5 is the better model for agentic coding, science-heavy terminal work and anything where recall matters. It costs roughly twice as much per finished task as GLM-5.3, not four and a half times, and it is worth the difference for the workloads both vendors advertise.

GLM-5.3 is the right choice when the weights have to be yours, when the workload is long-context reasoning or on-call triage, or when the job is cyber-defence. It is a genuine frontier-adjacent open model at a genuinely low price, and its biggest weakness — science-terminal work at 9.5% — is narrow enough that a workload-specific evaluation will tell you in an afternoon whether it matters to you.

GLM-5.4, the model in the title, is not part of the decision. It is a version number with no release behind it, and if Z.ai ships it the arithmetic above is what it will have to beat.

模型选型中最昂贵的错误，是拿价目表来比较，而不是比较最终完成的任务。Claude Opus 5.5 每百万输入 token 收费 4 美元，每百万输出 token 收费 20 美元。GLM-5.3——Z.ai 实际发布的模型，也是任何输入“GLM-5.4”的人真正在找的模型——收费分别为 1.40 美元和 4.40 美元。单看标价，这个中国开放权重模型的价格大约只有五分之一。但按 Artificial Analysis 自己对完成一项任务所需成本的测算，这一差距缩小到了 2 倍。真正构成这次对比核心的，是这一差距的缩小，而不是价目表。

首先，说说名称。GLM-5.4 并不存在。Z.ai 的文档索引将 GLM-5.3 和 GLM-5.3-Flash 列为当前文本模型，该实验室的 Hugging Face 组织中没有名称含“5.4”的仓库，而且 11 月 19 日在 Hub 上进行全文搜索没有任何结果。这个编号只是一个搜索词，并非已发布版本。GLM-5.3 于 2026 年 8 月发布——按 Artificial Analysis 的发布日期是 8 月 18 日，权重自 8 月 25 日起在 Hub 上提供——下文所有说法所指的正是这个模型。

## GLM-5.3 是什么，以及它的价格是多少

GLM-5.3 是 Z.ai 的开放权重文本旗舰模型。它与 GLM-5.2 使用相同的基座模型，所有提升都来自后训练，因此许可证和架构保持不变，改进也恰好集中在两个地方：复杂编程和长时程智能体任务。它拥有 100 万 token 上下文、128K 最大输出、纯文本输入，并且推理无法关闭——共有三档推理强度，低、高和最高，默认使用最高。

• 价格 — Claude Opus 5.5 输入 $4.00 / 输出 $20.00 / 缓存读取 $0.20，对比 GLM-5.3 $1.40 / $4.40。

• 权重——仅提供封闭 API，还是在 Hugging Face 上以 Apache 式开放发布、可下载并自托管。

• 上下文 — 两者均为 1M tokens，两者最大输出均为 128K。

• 推理强度控制——Opus 5.5 运行无法禁用的自适应思考，默认 medium，而 GLM-5.3 的推理始终开启，默认 max。

• 智能指数 —— 在 v5.0.1 修订版上为 59.1 对 31.7，相差 27.4 分。

• 每项 Index 任务的成本 — 10.04 美元 vs 5.01 美元，差距为 2 倍，而非标价所暗示的 4.5 倍。

• 模态 — 文本与图像输入 vs 仅文本输入。

## 为什么4.5倍的价格优势会变成2倍的成本优势

Artificial Analysis 让两个模型跑完了同一套 Index 测试，并统计了各自消耗的 token 数量。Claude Opus 5.5 在整个测试套件中生成了 2.18 亿个输出 token，GLM-5.3 则生成了 1.35 亿个。这与大多数人的预期方向相反——在这里，价格更高的模型反而是更啰嗦的那个——但真正关键的比例是相对于价格的比例，GLM-5.3 那 1.6 倍的 token 优势，远不足以抵消它在另一方向上 4.5 倍的每 token 价格优势。

像做预算那样算这笔账。在两项模型消耗相同 token 数的任务上，GLM-5.3 便宜 4.5×。实际上，Opus 5.5 每消耗 1 个 token，GLM-5.3 约消耗 0.62 个 token，因此在计入输入 token 之前，有效比率接近 2.8×；而实测的每任务成本为 $5.01 对 $10.04，使其达到 2×。这仍然是实实在在的节省——大约一半——但一半与五分之一是不同的决策。一个按标价做预算、却拿到 2× 账单的团队，会构建错误的商业论证。

有一个二阶效应值得特别指出，因为它让不止一个团队栽了跟头：GLM-5.3 的推理默认设置为 max。如果迁移只替换模型 ID，却保持推理默认值不变，就会得到该模型最昂贵、最慢的配置，而冗长恰恰就源于此。Z.ai 自己的迁移说明明确指出，不再支持禁用推理，并且 low必须刻意设置。

## 能力差距是真实存在的，而且并不均衡。

27 分的指数差距听起来足以直接淘汰，而在通用知识工作中，这几乎确实如此。但各基准测试的分数沿着一条比综合分数更重要的分界线，将这两个模型区分开来。以下所有数据均来自 Artificial Analysis，使用同一测试框架，且两个模型均处于各自的最高强度设置。

• Terminal-Bench 4.0 — 59.6% 对比 41.9%。在智能体终端任务上相差 18 个百分点。

• FrontierCode-AA 2.0 — 46.4% 对 21.6%。Opus 5.5 达到 GLM-5.3 的两倍以上。

• Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 — 59.0% 对 9.5%。这是榜单上最大的差距，堪称一场碾压。

• HLE-Diamond — 67.9% 对比 17.9%。

• AA-Omniscience — 准确率为 65.5% 时为 48.1，而准确率为 32.3% 时为 6.0。

• GDPval-AA v2.1 — 1866 Elo 对 1655，是该组中差距最小的，为 211 分。

• ITBench-SRE — 38.2% 对 46.1%，这是 GLM-5.3 少数胜出的场景之一。

• LCR（长上下文推理）——84.7% 对 79.7%。

这个规律是：GLM-5.3 在长上下文推理和站点可靠性任务上表现稳健，但在科学密集型终端工作和知识回忆上表现不佳。如果你的工作负载是对长上下文进行文档分析，27 分的综合得分会夸大这一差距。如果是在不熟悉的代码仓库上进行智能体编程——这正是两家厂商都在宣传的场景——综合得分则会低估这一差距。

## Z.ai 发布的厂商对比表比较的是 Opus 4.8，而不是 Opus 5.5

在信任你在任何图表中看到的 GLM 与 Claude 对比数据之前，这一点值得了解。Z.ai 的 GLM-5.3 模型卡中有一张基准测试表，包含“Opus 4.8”列和“Fable 5 (w/ fallback)”列。Claude Opus 5.5 在 GLM-5.3 发布五周后推出，并未出现在其中。这并非不诚实——该表是在 5.3 发布时制作的，当时 Opus 5.5 尚不存在——但这确实意味着大多数人正在寻找的那项对比从未被任何一家厂商发布过，而目前唯一可得的同一测试框架下的数据，就是上面那些独立数据。

Z.ai 自己公布的数据里，确实有一项说法值得认真对待，因为它指向了这款开放权重模型真正的强项：在其漏洞发现基准 CyberGym 上，GLM-5.3 的得分为 84.5，而 Opus 4.8 为 78.1。模型卡将这一提升描述为"涌现"——随着后训练规模的扩大，网络能力的提升速度超出了团队的预期——而利用类基准相比 GLM-5.2 翻了一倍还多。Anthropic 于 9 月 29 日发布了一份关于 GLM-5.3 网络能力的分析，而厂商通常不会对竞争对手的开放权重发布做这种事。如果你的工作是防御性安全工具，那么这正是开放模型真正领先的一个维度，也是开放权重最重要的一个维度：你可以在自己的基础设施上运行分类器，而不必把与漏洞利用沾边的提示词发送到别人的 API。

## 开放权重真正改变决策的地方

以上所有内容都是能力与成本比较，而在这两方面，Claude Opus 5.5 在大多数工作中都胜出。GLM-5.3 仍会被部署的原因与这两者都无关：而是因为 5.3 系列模型可以下载、在你自己的网关后面运行，并且从不离开你的网络。

有三种具体情况会让这一点比 27 个指数点更重要。受监管的数据无法跨越司法辖区边界，在这种情况下，选择要么是 GLM-5.3，要么别无选择。在大规模分类场景中，对基础模型进行 3 亿参数的微调，就能在你的标签上以远低于每次调用成本的成本胜过通用模型。还有网络安全相关工具，在这里，基准优势与自托管要求指向同一方向。

至于其他所有情况，诚实的建议是让路由决策保持低成本。两个模型都在同一个 OrcaRouter 密钥上——anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 和 z-ai/glm-5.3——按供应商标价 0% 加价，这一点对 Z.ai 一方比对 Anthropic 一方更重要，因为 Z.ai 在 2026 年两次调整了这条产品线的价格。把高并发、低风险的批次路由到 GLM-5.3，把规划循环交给 Opus 5.5，并让故障转移来兜底低价层供应商偶尔状态不佳的情况。路由 DSL 让这一切只需改一次配置，而无需维护两套集成；预算里该填的是混合后的每任务成本，而不是任何一个标价。

## 答案，名字已定

Claude Opus 5.5 是更适合智能体编程、科学密集型终端工作以及任何重视召回效果的场景的模型。每完成一项任务，它的成本约为 GLM-5.3 的两倍，而不是四倍半；对于两家厂商宣传的工作负载来说，这一差价是值得的。

当模型权重必须掌握在自己手中，当工作负载是长上下文推理或值班分诊，或者当任务是网络防御时，GLM-5.3 就是正确的选择。它是一款真正接近前沿水平的开源模型，价格也确实低廉；其最大弱点——科学终端类工作仅 9.5%——范围足够狭窄，以至于一次针对具体工作负载的评估就能在一个下午告诉你，它对你是否重要。

GLM-5.4，即标题中的那个模型，并不在讨论范围内。它只是一个背后并无实际发布的版本号，而如果 Z.ai 真的发布它，那么上面这套算术就是它必须超越的基准。

# Zhipu AI (ZHIPU) Stock Price Prediction: JPMorgan stays constructive as futures lean oversold

Zhipu AI (ZHIPU) is trading at $45.82 after a 5.29% 24-hour gain, but the broader setup still looks technically fragile with price below the short- and medium-term moving averages. JPMorgan maintai...

## What changed

Zhipu AI (ZHIPU) is trying to stabilize after a sharp slide that still leaves the contract below every major short- and medium-term trend marker. The current price of $45.82 sits under the 7-day SMA at $49.14, the 20-day SMA at $55.43, and the 50-day SMA at $65.91, which keeps the broader trend structure bearish even after the 24-hour rebound.

At the same time, JPMorgan held its Overweight rating on November 18, 2026 and argued that fundamentals remain solid despite weaker sentiment. The bank pointed to commercialization progress in GLM, partnerships with cloud providers, and improving margins, and said the market may be too pessimistic. It also set a HK$1,200 target.

## Technical read: oversold, but not repaired

The tape is showing an oversold-but-not-yet-trending-favorable profile. Daily RSI at 35.20 is still in neutral-to-weak territory, while stochastic readings at 15.81 and 12.65 show momentum remains compressed. The MACD histogram at 0.0000, with MACD and signal both at -5.7048, suggests downside momentum has stalled rather than reversed.

Price is also pressing the lower end of the Bollinger structure. The lower band is $43.40, and %B at 0.1007 puts ZHIPU close to lower-band support. That matters because the next failure point is nearby: immediate support is $43.37, with strong support at $40.93. On the upside, the first test is $47.73, then $49.65.

Volatility remains elevated, with ATR(14) at $5.66. That makes intraday swings meaningful relative to spot and increases the chance that either support or resistance gets swept before any clean trend develops.

## Positioning: shorts are paying, but bulls are crowded

Binance perpetual futures show a mixed read beneath the surface. The funding rate is -0.0331%, which means shorts are paying longs and often reflects a market leaning bearish enough to support a squeeze if price starts to lift. But open interest fell 7.57% over 24 hours to $11.3 million, pointing to position closing and liquidations rather than fresh conviction.

The account split is heavily long-biased: Binance global accounts are 79.8% long versus 20.2% short, and top-trader accounts are 83.2% long versus 16.8% short, both at 2026-11-18 13:00 UTC. That is not a clean bullish signal by itself; it does suggest that if support breaks, the market is exposed to a crowded-side unwind. Taker flow, however, is still weak: the 1-hour taker buy/sell ratio is 0.6132, with sell volume exceeding buy volume, so aggressive selling pressure has not disappeared.

## What would change the setup

For ZHIPU to shift from a bear-market bounce into something more durable, it first needs to reclaim the pivot at $45.29 and then clear $47.73 with volume. A close back above the 20-day SMA at $55.43 would be a more meaningful technical repair. Until then, the base case remains a market that is oversold, but still trading under pressure.

On the downside, losing $43.37 would hand control back to the bears and expose $40.93. With the moving-average stack still bearish and taker flow still negative, support levels matter more than the recent 24-hour bounce.

GLM.description: Zhiyuan Institute 发布了面向国产 Token 工厂的端到端推理优化方案，针对华为 Ascend 910C 集群上的 Zhipu GLM-5.3 和 GLM-5.3-Flash 模型进行了深度优化。
GLM.content:
绿涨红跌

涨跌幅与 K 线开盘时间

24 小时制

智源 FlagOS 优化华为昇腾 910C 集群上的 GLM-5.3 推理

关键要点

智源研究院通过 LI 量化融合，将内核延迟从 18.03 微秒降至 2.04 微秒，使 Huawei Ascend 910C 的解码阶段延迟缩短至原来的约 1/9。

FlagOS 生态整合了 21 家芯片企业和 86 家合作伙伴，覆盖 35 款 AI 芯片，累计收录 1,454 个开源 Triton 算子，其中 800 个算子在国产芯片上的性能达到原生性能的 80%。

智源通过 Prefill-Decode 分离架构和跨域缓存优化，使老款 Ascend 910B 服务器支持 GLM-5.3-Flash 的 100 万上下文，并将首 token 延迟降低 81.4%。

Zhiyuan Institute 发布了面向国产 Token 工厂的端到端推理优化方案，针对华为 Ascend 910C 集群上的 Zhipu GLM-5.3 和 GLM-5.3-Flash 模型进行了深度优化。这项计划旨在解决中国 AI 基础设施中的一个关键缺口：将闲置、异构且难以使用的国产算力，转化为可量化、高可靠性的标准化生产能力。

FlagOS 是 Zhiyuan 与高校及芯片厂商合作开发、历时四年的开源系统软件栈，目前已整合 21 家芯片企业和 86 家生态合作伙伴，覆盖 35 款 AI 芯片。FlagOS 生态由四个核心层组成：通用算子库 FlagGems、训练推理并行框架 FlagScale、统一编译器 FlagTree，以及统一通信库 FlagCX。该项目在九个算子库中累计收录了超过 1,454 个开源 Triton 算子，其中近 800 个算子在至少 5 款国产芯片上的性能达到原生算子性能的 80% 以上。

面向 Ascend 910C 上 GLM-5.3 的微秒级内核优化

对于追求盈利的商业 Token 工厂而言，模型的“功能性”只是基础要求；降低延迟、提升吞吐量，对服务质量和利润率至关重要。在此次联合发布的方案中，Zhiyuan 团队针对华为 Ascend 910C 集群上的 GLM-5.3 和 GLM-5.3-Flash 模型，将优化深入到微秒级内核层面。

大型语言模型推理在两个阶段面临不同的瓶颈：计算密集型的 Prefill 阶段和内存访问密集型的 Decode 阶段。在 Prefill 阶段，针对 GLM-5.3-Flash 的混合注意力架构，团队重构了大、小计算路径，协调芯片的向量计算单元和矩阵计算单元并行工作，同时避免中间结果频繁进行片外传输。在输入长度为 81,920、并发请求数为 16 的测试中，批量吞吐量提升了 3.41%；在 25.6 万超长输入下，TTFT p50 降低了 4.94%。

在 Decode 阶段，内存访问带宽是最主要的限制因素，团队对分散的算子进行了深度融合。通过 LI 量化回写技术，团队将原本分步执行的动态量化、尺度转换和 HBM 缓存回写合并为一个内核。在 910C 微基准测试中，这项改动将原生链路延迟从 18.03 微秒压缩至 2.04 微秒，提速近 9 倍。结合针对小批量输入的向量路径定制后，端到端商业场景测试显示，Decode 阶段的 ITL 降低了 10% 以上，TPOT 降低了 8% 以上。

在老一代 Ascend 910B 硬件上实现 100 万上下文支持

除了提升新一代芯片的性能，中国的数据中心还面临一个更迫切的挑战：如何管理已部署的存量设备。大量 Ascend 910B 服务器已投入使用，但在支持具有百万 token（100 万）上下文窗口的新一代模型时，面临 GPU 显存和算力的双重限制。

Zhiyuan 团队在其内部 BAAI Token Hub 上搭建了 Prefill-Decode 分离推理集群，调度 48 张老一代 910B 卡，稳定运行支持 100 万上下文的 GLM-5.3-Flash 服务。该配置将 32 张卡划分为 4 个 Prefill 域，用于处理长序列输入；另外 16 张卡组成 8 个 Decode 域，专注于保障多并发流式输出。该服务已连续稳定运行两周，在线 TTFT P50 保持在约 2.3 秒，TPOT P50 稳定在 22 毫秒。

通过重构缓存和传输路径，系统效率显著提升。团队在框架插件层启用了跨 Prefill 域的 Prefix Cache 复用，将缓存划分为三个存储层级：本地 GPU 内存、专用主机内存和共享主机内存；同时结合分段 SDMA 优化，将分散的内存页合并为连续传输片段，提高 PCIe 带宽利用率。测试数据显示，该方案将前缀命中率从 82.65% 提升至 94.15%，并在缓存复用阶段将首 token 延迟中位数从 16.63 秒降至 3.10 秒，降幅达 81.4%。

多芯片横向验证与生态支持

Zhiyuan 强调，统一软件栈的价值不能仅凭单一芯片验证。峰会上公布的多芯片横向测试结果显示，FlagOS 2.2 在 Pinecone Technology 810E 上将 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 的推理性能提升了 77% 至 82%，实现 16 路并发可用，最高支持 80 路并发，单请求解码速度为 136.2 tok/s。在 Hygon BW1100 上，GLM-5.3-Flash 的推理性能提升超过 25%，单路多并发下的吞吐量超过 80 TPS。

从底层算子库和编译器到跨芯片调度插件，Zhiyuan 作为一级战略合作伙伴参与了此次联合发布，旨在将开源社区积累的优化能力直接带给一线 Token 工厂和企业用户。Zhiyuan 负责人表示，研究院和开源社区发挥着“保驾护航”的作用：无论用户运行的是已长期部署的老旧集群、新部署的新一代芯片，还是未来的新型硬件架构，都无需担心无法运行最新模型。随着算力竞争转向衡量“有效 token”，开放、可复用的系统软件基础正成为国产算力摆脱周期性限制的关键支点。

关键信息

Zhiyuan 的 FlagOS 生态整合了 21 家芯片企业和 86 家生态合作伙伴，覆盖 35 款 AI 芯片

九个算子库累计收录了超过 1,454 个开源 Triton 算子

近 800 个算子在至少 5 款国产芯片上的性能达到原生算子性能的 80% 以上

GLM-5.3-Flash Prefill 阶段在输入长度为 81,920、并发请求数为 16 的测试中，批量吞吐量提升了 3.41%

Kimi.content:
MAI Code 2 与 Kimi K3.1 Pro：定价策略对比及已公布基准

关键要点

微软的 MAI Code 2 于 2026 年 11 月 17 日发布，输入代币价格为每 100 万个代币 0.50 美元，输出代币价格为每 100 万个代币 2.50 美元，促销价格将于 2027 年 5 月 17 日结束。

根据 Artificial Analysis 的数据，Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Intelligence Index 5.0.1 版中得分为 46，在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 中得分为 65.7%，任务完成时间为 38.4 分钟。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 提供了 1.56 TB 的 MXFP4 格式模型权重，并支持依据定制许可证进行自托管；而 MAI Code 2 仅限 GitHub Copilot 订阅用户访问。

Microsoft 于 2026 年 11 月 17 日推出 MAI Code 2，公布了定价，但未发布具体的基准测试成绩；Moonshot AI 于 2026 年 10 月 24 日宣布推出、并于 11 月 4 日开放使用的 Kimi K3.1 Pro，则同时公布了定价和 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 评分 46。MAI Code 2 的价格为每百万输入代币 $0.50、每百万输出代币 $2.50；相比之下，Kimi K3.1 Pro 的相应价格为 $2.00 和 $10.00——四倍的定价差距反映了两者截然不同的商业和技术策略。这一比较揭示了一个关键取舍：Microsoft 给出的比率和能力声明无法独立验证，而 Moonshot 则公布了可衡量的性能数据，并提供可下载的模型权重。

Microsoft 的发布文档列出了四项编码基准测试——DeepSWE 1.1、Terminal Bench 2.1、SWE-Atlas 和 FrontierCode v1.1——但只公布了平均性能比率，没有公布各项基准测试的通过率。其中三项基准测试通过 GitHub Copilot CLI 在 Microsoft 内部评测平台 MSBench 上运行，禁用了子代理，并将模型设为最高推理强度。FrontierCode 的得分来自 Artificial Analysis。公布的结果称，MAI Code 2 在四项基准测试中的平均表现达到 Claude Opus 5.5 的 96%，成本为其 5%；达到 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 98%，成本为其 40%。在盲测前端评估中，评审者有 64% 的时间更偏好 MAI Code 2 的输出。Microsoft 的发布文档和模型页面均未列出通过率、参数数量或输出上限。截至 2026 年 11 月 18 日，Artificial Analysis 上没有 MAI Code 2 的条目，因此其能力尚无独立验证。Microsoft 明确表示，这些模型“尚未针对更难的问题进行调优，例如基础科学研究和超长周期的智能体工作”。

MAI Code 2 的定价结构与访问限制

GitHub 以完整精度列出了 MAI Code 2 的费率。输入价格为每百万代币 $0.50，而 Kimi K3.1 Pro 为 $2.00，因此 MAI 的价格仅为其四分之一。输出价格为每百万代币 $2.50，对比 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的 $10.00，仍保持四倍价差。缓存输入价格方面，MAI Code 2 每百万代币为 $0.025，Kimi K3.1 Pro 为 $0.20，前者仅为后者的八分之一；GitHub 未公布这两款模型的缓存写入费用。MAI Code 2 的上下文窗口长达 100 万代币，但仅能在 Visual Studio Code 和 Copilot CLI 中使用；Kimi K3.1 Pro 则通过 Moonshot 的 API 提供 1,048,576 个代币的上下文窗口。两家厂商均未单独公布输出上限；所列数字代表上下文窗口，而非生成限制。

Microsoft 的促销定价将于 2027 年 5 月 17 日到期，之后 MAI Code 2 的价格将调整为每百万输入代币 $1.00、每百万输出代币 $5.00，其价格优势将减半：新鲜代币为 2 倍，缓存代币为 4 倍。缓存输入价格主导着智能体工作流的成本，因为此类工作流会在每一轮重复传入固定的系统提示词、稳定的工具架构和代码仓库前缀。当前 MAI 的缓存代币价格为每百万 $0.025，而 Kimi 为 $0.20，因此在主导账单的项目上，价差大于标题所示的四倍。从 2027 年 5 月 17 日起，缓存费率将升至 $0.05，而 Moonshot 的费率保持不变，缓存代币的价格优势将缩小至 4 倍。MAI Code 2 仅通过 GitHub Copilot 订阅提供，包括 Pro、Pro+、Max、Business 和 Enterprise 套餐。较小的 MAI Code 2 Flash 变体则通过 OpenAI 兼容的 Responses API，在 Microsoft Foundry 中以有限访问预览版的形式提供 API 接口。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 的实测性能与独立验证

Kimi K3.1 Pro 于 2026 年 10 月 24 日发布的文档显示，该模型在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上取得 65.7%，排名第二，落后于得分为 66.4% 的 Claude Opus 5.5。这是在一项当前基准测试中公布的实际百分比，厂商在发布当天就予以披露，没有人为夸大。在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 5.0.1 版中，Kimi K3.1 Pro 得分为 46，远高于同类模型 23 的中位数。Artificial Analysis 计算得出，Kimi K3.1 Pro 每项 Intelligence Index 任务的成本为 $3.68，每项任务耗时 38.4 分钟，输出速度为每秒 31 个代币，首个代币耗时 157.8 秒。该任务完成时间显著高于 Artificial Analysis 报告的每项任务 13.6 分钟中位数，因此 Kimi K3.1 Pro 更适合循环执行的智能体工作，而非交互式聊天。这些指标提供了量化基准，可用于评估某款模型是否适用于智能体工作流。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 的模型权重共计 1.56 TB，以 MXFP4 格式分为 96 个分片，于 2026 年 11 月 4 日发布并可供下载。其分发许可设有定制营收门槛，并非 Apache、MIT 或 OSI 批准的许可；这意味着“开放”指的是可审计性和自托管能力，而非不受限制的再分发权。对于安全审查和内部部署，这一区别影响重大；对于计划再分发的产品，则需要仔细审查许可条款。OrcaRouter 将 Kimi K3.1 Pro 列为 kimi/kimi-k3.1-pro，输入价格为每百万代币 $2.00，输出价格为每百万代币 $10.00，按 Moonshot 公布的费率转售，不收取任何加价，因此费率变化会立即生效，无需等待转售商轮流调整价格。自动故障转移会将服务提供方一侧的速率限制转化为重试，而非中断长时间运行的智能体任务。

分发、可审计性与使用场景匹配

由于 MAI Code 2 唯一公布的使用途径是通过 GitHub Copilot 订阅，因此无法将其纳入目录式产品。这一限制迫使对比实验采用不同方式：一个候选模型在 Copilot 客户端内运行，另一个则通过 HTTP 端点执行。这是实验设计中的实际限制，并非微不足道的实现细节。该限制要求采用两层部署策略：将 Kimi K3.1 Pro 用于经过测量和预算规划的路径，其每项任务 $3.68 的成本和 38 分钟的完成时间都是已知的规划变量。对于已经使用 Copilot 的开发者，则部署 MAI Code 2，让他们试用，除现有席位许可外无需额外付费。之后，应根据直接的代码仓库测试结果，而非四项基准测试的平均值，来判断每项已完成任务的成本。

Microsoft 的定价策略面向已经订阅 Copilot、希望在现有工具中使用更便宜代币的团队。Moonshot 的方案则面向需要模型可审计性、自托管能力或跨基础设施资产可移植性的团队。两款模型都不意味着性价比低，而是服务于不同类型的买家。四倍的代币价格差距反映了两者的真实差异：一方提供可下载权重、独立性能测量、已公布的基准测试，以及允许自托管的许可框架；另一方则采用专有托管、促销代币定价，且能力声明依赖内部基准测试和厂商给出的比率。

关键事实

MAI Code 2 和 Kimi K3.1 Pro 在定价和上下文窗口方面有何不同？

MAI Code 2 的价格为每百万输入代币 $0.50、每百万输出代币 $2.50（自 2027 年 5 月 17 日起将调整为 $1.00 和 $5.00），上下文窗口为 100 万代币，但仅可在 GitHub Copilot CLI 和 Visual Studio Code 中使用。Kimi K3.1 Pro 的价格为每百万输入代币 $2.00、每百万输出代币 $10.00，通过 Moonshot 的 API 提供 1,048,576 个代币的上下文窗口。缓存输入价格方面，MAI Code 2 每百万代币为 $0.025，Kimi K3.1 Pro 则为 $0.20。对于会反复传入系统提示词和代码仓库上下文的智能体工作流，缓存输入成本占账单的大头，因此尽管 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的上下文窗口更大，其缓存价格仍显著更高。

两款模型分别有哪些性能指标？

2026年11月12日，Decision Index——追踪 TypeSafe's Jev 开放复现的社区排行榜——将Karpo Decision 31B置于其 Full score 榜首，73.9，为307个条目中最高。同一周，开始流传一种说法：这个模型——Google 开源的 Gemma 4 31B 的微调版——胜过 Google 自家的Gemini Decision 1。这两种说法中，只有一种读者今天可以核查，而它们之间的差别正是整个故事所在。将 Karpo 列为首位的榜单是公开的、有日期的，并且可从该实验室发布的 45 MB 结果文件中复现。与 Gemini Decision 1 的正面对决从未进行过：这两个模型并不共享同一个排行榜，而且用于给它们评分的工具也不是同一种工具。

前半段之所以奇怪，不在於分數，而在於圍繞它的沉默。Karpo 背後的加坡公司 MachinePulse Pte. Ltd. 於 2026 年 11 月 5 日建立了 Hugging Face 儲存庫，同日在 GitHub 發布了推論儲存庫，並於 11 月 12 日推出五個較小的同系列模型——12B、9B、4B、2B 和 0.8B。截至本文撰寫時，沒有產品頁面、沒有部落格文章、沒有定價、沒有模型公告，也沒有 API。公司自家網站上，所有應該放這些內容的路徑都回傳 404。Karpo 僅以權重、README、Python 套件和排行榜上的一列存在。本文要談的是，這四樣東西能告訴你什麼、不能告訴你什麼。

## 這些日期，以及它們為何比往常更重要

儲存庫建立時間戳記為 2026 年 11 月 5 日 15:33 UTC。GitHub 推論程式碼則在二十二分鐘後建立。Decision Index 執行資料集——也就是讓 73.9 得以可稽核的那項東西——是在 11 月 6 日 05:18 UTC 上傳的。README 到 11 月 16 日仍持續在編輯，最後兩次提交只改了一行著作權聲明和一段授權條款陳述，其餘什麼都沒動。

那是一個問世兩週的模型，擁有活躍的程式碼倉庫，卻沒有正式發布。它不是外洩，也不是某個較舊東西的改名：權重是新的，授權檔案是新的，而且六個模型的家族是在一個下午內推送上去的。它是什麼呢？就是一個決定先發布產物、再進行行銷的實驗室。

## 73.9 究竟衡量的是什麼

Decision Index 目前是 0.4.1 版。其 Full 分數由該委員會的維護者透過私有測試計算：約 60% 的任務取自與公開測試套件相同的技能，40% 則來自公開測試套件未涵蓋的領域。Karpo 那一列顯示 Full 為 73.9，其中同技能部分為 70.7，新領域部分為 78.6。最後這兩個數字的順序並不尋常——模型通常在不熟悉的領域上，表現會比在其受調校過的技能上更差——而卡片未加評論地呈現了這一點。

榜單會將與領先者差距在 0.9 分以內的模型並列同一名次，因此 Karpo 並非獨占第一。GLiDE 27B 以 73.4 分並列第 1 名。緊隨其後的是 REAX 1.3（72.6）、Logits Sigma-1 Duo（72.3）、Copernicus-31B（72.1）與 KnowLine 31B Gen1.5（71.9）。這是競爭激烈的領先群，而非一枝獨秀。

卡片上的第二個數字 75.05 來源不同，也值得以不同方式解讀。那是公開指數，來自 MachinePulse 自行執行官方評分套件的結果——140,178 個已評分請求，其中九個遭到拒絕，因為單一問題加上其狀態超過了 32,768 個 token 的視窗。董事會採用了該次執行結果。相較於一般廠商數字，值得更信任它的原因在於執行目錄是公開的：results.jsonl.gz、逐請求分數檔、環境清單。任何人都能重新執行套件並進行比較。董事會自身的採用即是審查步驟。這比大多數發布聲明所達到的標準更嚴格，但仍不等同於由獨立實驗室在其自有硬體上對模型評分。

那麼，會有兩個標籤，且不應將它們合併：Full 分數是由第三方根據私有測試計算而得；公開指數則是由第一方根據公開測試套件計算並採用。兩者都不是一般意義上的廠商基準測試。兩者也都不是 Artificial Analysis。

## 為什麼「beats Gemini Decision 1」還不是一項經過實測的陳述

Gemini Decision 1 有一個分數。Artificial Analysis 在 Decision Index v2.1 上給它 65.98 分，該指數由六項評估綜合而成，權重涵蓋文件決策、工具呼叫、知識、推理與不變性。在那個榜單上，它在 AA 排名的決策模型中位列第十一，低於 74.85 的 d1.2-ultra、72.62 的 Drex Max v1.1 與 72.58 的 SubQ Snap 1.2，高於 62.07 的 Microsoft-Decision-1。評分是 AA 的，使用 AA 的硬體，且執行成本為每百萬項任務 345 美元。

Karpo 完全沒有出現在那個看板上。Artificial Analysis 沒有它的頁面，也沒有它的列。Gemini Decision 1 也沒有出現在收錄 Karpo 的 Decision Index 追蹤器上——那個看板是公開重現項目的登記冊，而 Google 的模型是封閉、僅供 API 使用的產品，沒有可供重現的權重。

所以，大家所做的比較，是根據兩個組織在兩套套件上產生的兩個數字推論而來；而這兩套套件的工作任務組成不同、私有測試占比不同，評分公式也不同。無論從哪個經得起方法論檢驗的角度來看，73.9 都不比 65.98 大。如果明天把這兩者放進同一套工具裡跑，Karpo 很可能會贏——它的分類別表現很強——但沒有人跑過，而目前的那個頭條結論，只是一個披著結果外衣的假設。

還有一點更值得知道，因為這點不利於那個說法，而不是支持它。在追蹤器的五項類別細分中，Karpo 最弱的是知識與推理，機率校正技能值為 65.5；最強的是工具與自動化，為 88.4。在 AA 的排行榜上，Gemini Decision 1 幾乎擊敗所有對手的單一組成項目，就是知識項目：在 AA-Omniscience 上拿到 66.3，是此處受檢四個模型中最高的。Google 模型最強的地方，正是 Gemma 微調模型相對最弱的地方。在那裡，正面對決會是一場真正的較量，而不是一面倒，而這正是為什麼不應把未進行的比較報導為勝利。

## 卡片中比排名更有趣的部分

Karpo 不是具備 JSON 模式的聊天模型。它是一種讀出機制。問題中的每個選項都會獲得一個選項代碼，線性頭會在固定槽位對 255 個代碼評分，然後對問題實際提供的選項進行 softmax。不會生成任何內容，因此答案始終是你提供的其中一個選項，而輸出成本在結構上為零。

這套架構值得用一段來說明，因為它解釋了延遲。一個請求是一個狀態加上任意數量的問題，並編碼成單一序列：問題在前，接著是狀態，然後每個問題各一個分支。分支注意力讓一個分支能讀取共享區塊與自身，絕不會讀取另一個分支。狀態只計算一次。因此，針對同一張發票的一百個問題，成本大約是對該發票進行一次處理，而不是一百次。

• 參數 — 以 bf16 表示為 31.3B，外加一個 255 × 5,376 的 fp32 讀出層；磁碟上約 62.5 GB。

• 上下文 — 每個序列 32,768 個 token；較長的請求會按問題拆分，每個部分都攜帶完整狀態，而仍然無法容納的問題會被拒絕，而不是被截斷。

• 輸入 — 文字、JSON 與圖片；螢幕截圖可透過 state.viewport_screenshot 或資料 URL 傳入。

• 題型 — 選擇題，最多 255 個選項，noul 用於是非題，評分 用於有序等級。

• 介面 — 以 System One 形式提供的 Python API 與 HTTP 伺服器，POST /v1/systemone。

• 授權條款 — 權重與程式碼採用 Apache-2.0，並在儲存庫中一併附上 Gemma 4 本身的授權條款。

在追蹤器的參考硬體上、以單一 GPU 一次處理一個請求所測得的延遲，中位數為 94 毫秒。這個速度還不足以在每一回合發出二十次小型呼叫的逐步代理迴圈中做到讓人察覺不到，但已足以支撐一個每次對話只觸發少數幾次的工具呼叫閘門。這張模型卡另外回報了 4.8 個百分點的校準誤差，而這正是部署與否真正取決於的數字：準確率告訴你最高分答案有多常是對的，校準則告訴你附加在它上面的機率是否能拿來設閾值。

## 尚未確認的部分，直白說明

沒有價格。不是「上市前暫不公開」——沒有價目表、沒有託管端點、沒有主控台、沒有試用。如果你今天想要 Karpo Decision 31B，你得下載 62.5 GB，並用該儲存庫自帶的載入器在自己的 GPU 上執行。把檢查點當成一般聊天模型載入，並不會重現它的回答；分支注意力與讀出機制兩者都不可或缺。

沒有獨立評分。Decision Index 是非官方且由社群維護的。它謹慎、紀錄完善，且對方法異常透明；它不是 Artificial Analysis，也未被要求在自身硬體上為這個模型評分。最有力的第三方要素是，其維護者在廠商從未見過的測試上計算出 Full 分數。

除了 README 本身的描述之外，沒有任何廠商聲明說明這個模型是為何而打造：代理在每一步所做的小型判斷——要呼叫工具還是先詢問、要點擊頁面上的哪個元素、某項退貨是否符合某項政策的資格。那段描述是實驗室的框架設定，並非經獨立驗證的範圍。

而且完全沒有公告。不是低調的那種，也不是更新日誌裡的一條記錄。權重上線兩週後，這家公司對外呈現的門面，是一個招聘頁面和另一條產品線。

## 這會讓想要嘗試它的團隊處於什麼境地

誠實的總結是，Karpo Decision 31B 是過去兩週最有趣、卻也最缺乏佐證的開放式決策模型。它的領先是真實的，但只是並列；它的公開指數可重現；它的私測分數確實來自第三方；而它的核心行銷主張——一個 Gemma 微調版本如今能在 Google 自家的決策模型上擊敗 Google——並未經實測。

對於已經在運行決策層的團隊而言，實務上的做法是影子部署，而不是遷移。保留目前承載生產流量的模型，對相同請求離線執行 Karpo，並比較機率而非標籤：4.8 個百分點的校準誤差意味著大約每二十個答案就有一個，其錯誤的信心程度高於其標示機率所暗示的；而你的閾值策略會決定這究竟會變成人工審查佇列，還是事故。如果你要為堆疊其餘部分標準化到單一端點，本週你實際能存取的模型就是目錄上的那些——Gemma 4 31B 本身，也就是 Karpo 的基礎模型，並透過one API 以供應商定價、無加價提供 200+ 模型，以及TypeSafe 的 Jev 1.14，也就是這整個開放復現排行榜打造來追趕的模型。Karpo 必須像其他模型一樣贏得它的位置：讓自己可被呼叫。

值得注意的不是 73.9，而是 MachinePulse 是否會在接下來一個月內推出產品頁、公布價格，並向 AA 提交。一家先在網站上線前發布權重的實驗室，通常是有原因的，而這個原因往往會以託管端點或轉向的形式出現。無論如何，AA 榜上的第一個獨立數字，將在一週內定案排行榜算術算了兩週仍未能定案的事。

# Microsoft ships Decision-1.1 and new MAI models, SiliconANGLE reports

The November 17 rollout pairs first-party models for coding, imaging and cyber work with Foundry changes that let teams set baselines for agent quality, safety, latency and cost, according to SiliconANGLE.

New generative artificial intelligence models and a set of updates to Foundry, Microsoft Corp.' s enterprise platform for grounding, testing and deploying AI applications and autonomous agents, went out on November 17, according to a report by SiliconANGLE's Kyt Dotson. Among the changes, Foundry IQ, part of Microsoft IQ, now ships an enterprise knowledge graph out of the box, pulling together unstructured and application data across an estate to provide context for building applications.[1]

Microsoft said Foundry now uses its existing transparency and observability features to build learning loops, with internal evaluations letting autonomous agents set baselines for quality, safety, latency and cost. Human annotations, now in preview, allow experts to rate and comment on agent traces based on business judgment, feeding results back into an improvement cycle alongside optimization tests and comparisons against real-world outcomes. Foundry can also adapt supported models to organizational data using reinforcement learning while it runs the compute, with each improvement becoming the next baseline.[1]

On the model side, Decision-1.1 is now generally available. Microsoft describes it as a fast, low-cost model for making routing, classification, prioritization, verification and workflow control decisions in software, returning calibrated confidence scores so applications can defer when uncertainty is high rather than reasoning through each step the way a large language model would. It follows Microsoft-Decision-1, released in October, and is built on a new base, Google LLC's Gemma 4 26B A4, adding multimodal support for images in instructions.[1]

Microsoft also extended its first-party MAI family. MAI-Code-2, aimed at demanding agentic coding, and MAI-Code-2-Flash, for high-volume everyday coding, are generally available on GitHub, with Code-2-Flash in private preview in Foundry. MAI-Image-2.7 and MAI-Image-2.7-Flash are in preview for editing and image generation, and MAI-Cyber-2-Flash is in preview inside Codename MDASH, the company's agentic code security system available to eligible organizations. Foundry's model pool now features a top 50 selection supported by a model router and AI Gateway, alongside more than 11,000 models from OpenAI Group PBC, Anthropic PBC, Meta Platforms Inc., Mistral AI SAS and the open-source community, which Microsoft said can be evaluated and deployed through the same continuous improvement workflow used for agents.[1]

# Insight launches AI agent store for business customers
Thu, 19th Nov 2026 (Today) 
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Insight has launched an online Agent Store for business customers, now generally available in 14 countries.

The store offers a catalogue of AI agents, platforms and related services designed to automate routine work across business functions. Customers can deploy the tools in days or weeks rather than months, either as standalone products or alongside consulting, implementation and managed services.

The launch adds six new agentic products to Insight's AI portfolio, bringing the total in its library to 15. Nine products were introduced earlier this year.

Products listed in the store include Insight AI Flight Academy, focused on training and change management, and TokenScope, which tracks token usage and AI consumption costs for finance teams. Insight said the offerings were first developed for clients or used internally in areas including security, finance and legal.

New products available at launch include Quote Advisor, which assesses pricing, inventory, freight and contract requirements to produce sourced quotes. NDA Review Agent is designed to review non-disclosure agreements against a company's legal policies, while Parts Order Assist helps warehouse, maintenance and field staff search catalogues and place parts orders.

Insight is positioning the store as a way for businesses to move AI projects beyond the pilot stage and into wider use. It said it applied the approach within its own operations before making the products available more broadly.

"Organisations are feeling the pressure to move AI from isolated pilots into production. As 'Client Zero', Insight has built a repeatable approach to help that's been proven first across our own organisation," said Jack Azagury, Chief Executive Officer of Insight.

"Having driven over 90% internal AI adoption, we know firsthand what it takes to deploy and scale agentic AI rapidly and responsibly. By combining the solutions offered in Agent Store with our consulting and managed services expertise, Insight is empowering clients to move from 'hype to how' with AI to deliver measurable results in their own enterprises and generate long-term value across every industry," Azagury said.

Early customer

Culligan International is the first external customer to implement Flight Academy, according to Insight. The water services company is using a mix of AI tools including Microsoft Copilot, Cowork, Copilot Studio, Azure and Microsoft Fabric, while also putting governance in place around cost and responsible use.

The deployment centres on workforce education and internal adoption rather than a single operational use case. Insight said the training-led approach is intended to help organisations build confidence in AI tools across teams and geographies.

"At Culligan, we believe technology doesn't transform a company - people do. Generative AI adoption is far ahead of the learning curve, and it's our responsibility to arm our teams with the best tools to lead now into the future," said Laura Walsh, Global Chief Information Officer of Culligan International.

"With our partners at Insight, we have prioritised AI education so our teams can confidently leverage AI productively and responsibly. We are leveraging Insight's best practice and have established a functional champions network which has turned AI adoption into an organic, community-led effort across functions and geographies," Walsh said.

Geographic reach

Agent Store is available in the United States and Canada, as well as Australia, New Zealand and Singapore. In Europe, the Middle East and Africa, it is available in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom.

The launch reflects growing competition among technology service providers to package AI software, advisory work and operational support into repeatable products that can be rolled out across large organisations. Rather than selling only bespoke AI projects, firms are increasingly assembling catalogues of narrower tools tied to functions such as legal review, quoting, training and cost control.

For customers, that model offers a way to buy more standardised AI products while still relying on outside support for deployment and governance. For providers such as Insight, it creates a route to extend consulting relationships into packaged software and managed services.

Insight's emphasis on internal use before external release also points to a wider market pattern, in which technology companies test automation tools in their own operations before offering them to clients. In this case, Insight said the products had been used across departments to simplify tasks and improve efficiency.

Insight said Agent Store is intended to widen access to automation for core business processes and support broader internal AI adoption, with products spanning legal, finance, operations and employee training.

# NFON launches AI Agent Studio for European businesses
Wed, 18th Nov 2026 (Today) 
SOFIAH NICHOLE SALIVIO News Editor

NFON has launched AI Agent Studio, now available across its European business communications portfolio.

The software is designed to let companies create AI agents for specific business tasks by describing requirements in natural language or building visual workflows. Users can test an initial version of an agent and then refine it step by step.

The launch expands the Munich-based company's AI offering beyond its existing visual development tools. It also gives sales partners a way to build tailored automation projects for customers in sectors including insurance, utilities, trades and local government.

AI Agent Studio combines two development approaches in one product. In Agent Mode, users describe the tasks an AI agent should carry out, how it should behave and any constraints it must observe. The system then generates a working version that can be tested and adjusted through further dialogue.

This mode includes controls that let users review proposed changes before approving them. Changes remain traceable and can be reversed if needed.

In Flow-Based Mode, users create agents through visual workflows and configure process steps manually. This is intended for cases where organisations want tighter, rule-based control over how a process runs and which actions an agent should take under defined conditions.

Use cases

NFON highlighted customer service as one example. An AI agent could answer frequently asked questions using stored information on products, services or internal processes, while also handling structured tasks such as receiving an enquiry, requesting missing information and passing details to the relevant team.

These agents can also be extended through links to other systems, including customer relationship management software and appointment management tools. For broader connections to third-party production systems, NFON offers integration through existing interfaces or custom-built links.

Projects that require more extensive work can be supported by NFON partners or the company's professional services team. The model is intended to make the product accessible through its existing European partner network rather than through direct deployment alone.

That channel strategy is central to the launch. Partners already use voicebots for tasks such as receiving insurance claims, processing meter readings for energy suppliers and pre-qualifying customer enquiries for tradespeople. AI Agent Studio is intended to extend those applications into wider process automation.

Partner focus

For resellers and integrators, the software is positioned as a way to move quickly from a customer requirement to an initial working application. Instead of starting with a large development project, partners can test ideas, show early versions to customers and refine them together.

NFON said it will support that approach with training and certification programmes, implementation examples and materials for customer advisory work. Depending on the project, partners may also handle technical integration.

The company framed the launch as part of a broader push to widen access to AI-led automation in the European market, especially among small and medium-sized businesses. It also pointed to larger organisations as potential users where more complex applications require stronger controls over how agents are created and changed.

"With AI Agent Studio we are consistently advancing our AI-solution portfolio," said Andreas Wesselmann, Chief Executive Officer, NFON.

"We are laying the foundations to grow in line with our customers' requirements and address an ever-wider range of operational tasks. In doing so, we are strengthening our role as a long-term technology partner for AI transformation in the European SME sector, while also providing the technological foundation for more complex applications in larger organisations."

Jana Richter said the company wants to make the technology easier to use. "With AI Agent Studio, we turn complex technology into a tool for everyday business. Using artificial intelligence for an enterprise's tasks and designing bespoke solutions should no longer require expert knowledge," said Jana Richter, Executive Vice President, Engineering, AI & Innovation, NFON.

"We aim to democratise advanced AI automation. It shouldn't be the technical barriers that determine what companies can achieve, but their ideas," she said.

# Google Labs Announces Product Agent “Stitch Loop”

この記事のポイント

- Google Labs has announced “Stitch Loop,” a long-running product agent that continuously improves products 24/7 by integrating with codebases and live metrics, serving as a new experimental feature for the UI design tool “Stitch.”
- An agent that connects to codebases and live metrics to autonomously identify issues that need fixing and continuously improves products around the clock until goals are achieved.
- Waitlist registration (stitch.google.com/loop/waitlist) is now open to all users globally.

On Wednesday, November 18, 2026 (local time), Google’s experimental projects division, Google Labs, announced “Stitch Loop,” a long-running product agent representing a new direction for the AI-native design platform “Google Stitch (Stitch).”

“Stitch Loop” is an agent that connects to codebases and live metrics to autonomously identify issues that need fixing, continuously improving products 24/7 until set goals are achieved. While conventional coding agents complete their role once a pull request (PR) is merged, post-production releases require ongoing improvements such as fixing vulnerabilities, speeding up checkouts, and identifying drop-off factors buried in noisy feedback.

To get started, users connect product context—such as logs, user behavior, and feedback—via “GitHub,” integrations with over 180 external services, custom MCP servers, or local CLI uploads. In addition to three default loops (Cybersecurity / Latency / Accessibility), users can add custom loops at any time, such as one aimed at improving checkout conversion rates.

Each loop operates autonomously through four steps: “Suggestions” (proposing opportunities for improvement to achieve goals), “Solutions” (presenting fixes including trade-offs, scopes, and design proposals), “Build” (writing code in an isolated cloud sandbox and creating pull requests with screenshots/videos), and “Reflect” (learning and improving accuracy by monitoring live data, followed by continuous monitoring after goals are met). Note that final approval authority always remains with the user; code is never merged automatically without reviewing the pull request.

Particularly in terms of security, the platform features a dedicated loop combining the cybersecurity capabilities of the cutting-edge AI model “Gemini 4 Carbon” with “CodeMender,” an autonomous code security improvement agent from the AI research lab Google DeepMind. It scans the codebase for vulnerabilities before incidents occur and generates pull requests with proposed fixes along with rationale.

Furthermore, “Stitch Loop” functions as a service layer for coding agents such as the agent execution infrastructure “Google Antigravity,” allowing persistent product context to be shared via Stitch CLI or MCP. It also integrates with “Slack,” enabling users to receive daily insight digests or create new loops simply by mentioning “@stitch.”

Waitlist registration (stitch.google.com/loop/waitlist) for “Stitch Loop” is now open to all users globally. Priority access will be provided to eligible “Google AI Ultra” members.
